# ui::EarlyPalette

Header: `winui/ui/themes/EarlyPalette.hpp`.

The colors of an early Windows scheme: ten in Windows 1.x, thirteen in Windows 2.x. The three 2.x-only colors are `std::optional` and empty in a Windows 1.x palette. Where the theme needs a border color and a 1.x palette has none, it uses [`window_frame`](#window_frame).

Every value in the four factories below is the one that Windows release shipped.

A palette is the input to [Theme::early()](theme.md#early), which derives the whole early-Windows theme from it. Replace the whole palette instead of single colors. The four palettes are four distinct looks, and mixing colors between them gives a scheme no Windows release had.

Example: 
```cpp
// The default Windows 2.03 color look for the whole window.
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::early(ui::EarlyPalette::windows_2x_color()));

// Windows 1.01 on a monochrome display. Its row has no border slots, so the window border
// is drawn in `window_frame`.
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::early(ui::EarlyPalette::windows_1x_mono()));
```

## windows_2x_color

```cpp
static EarlyPalette windows_2x_color()
```

Windows 2.03 on a color display: the default, and the one to pick if only one early-Windows palette is wanted. Windows 2.03 uses it on every color adapter. A cyan desktop and cyan menu bar, and a blue caption with white text over a white page.

## windows_2x_mono

```cpp
static EarlyPalette windows_2x_mono()
```

Windows 2.03 on a monochrome display, the same on every monochrome adapter.

## windows_1x_mono

```cpp
static EarlyPalette windows_1x_mono()
```

Windows 1.01 on a monochrome display: the safest single choice for a Windows 1.x look. All of that release's monochrome display drivers use these colors.

The three 2.x-only colors stay `nullopt`.

## windows_1x_color

```cpp
static EarlyPalette windows_1x_color()
```

Windows 1.01 on a color display, as its EGA drivers ship it: a red scroll-bar trough on a white window under a blue caption.

Photos of the Windows 1.01 retail box show yellow-green troughs and pale cyan windows instead, likely a scheme picked for the shot.
